newsitem.title: FRANCE: French TPS signs exclusive film deal with Milchan.
newsitem.headline: French TPS signs exclusive film deal with Milchan.

text.p: Television par Satellite (TPS), a French digital satellite television service operated by private TV station TF1, said on Wednesday it signed an exclusive deal to carry films made by U.S. producer Arnon Milchan's Regency Enterprises on its pay television service.
It said it will have exclusive rights to broadcast all films to be made by Regency, as well as its most recent feature films.
The accord covers first and second run and pay-per-view, a TPS spokeswoman said. She could give no monetary value for the deal.

The films will be broadcast on three cinema channels run by TPS, Cinestar 1, Cinestar 2 and Cinetoile, which also run on two French cable TV networks, and on TPS's Multivision pay-per-view service, it said.
Milchan, whose biggest successes were "Pretty Woman" and "JFK", is due to present his latest film, "L.A. Confidential", at the Cannes film festival later on Wednesday, the spokeswoman said.

TPS has said it is moving onto the offensive in its quest for film rights. It has just clinched its first pre-purchase deals, spending 13.5 million francs on pre-purchasing "Droit dans le Mur", a comedy by French actor Pierre Richard, and 16.5 million francs for "Voleur de Vie" with French actress Emmanuelle Beart.
